spec_notes: 370W available PoE with the default single PWR-C5-600WAC supply; power budget changes with PSU configuration. Fixed 1/10G uplinks. StackWise-80 requires optional stack hardware. Meraki cloud management is software- and license-dependent; cloud monitoring is not the same as management.

437W available PoE with one default PWR-C1-715WAC-P PSU. Uplinks describe the separately ordered C9300-NM-8X module, not included fixed ports. A modular uplink does not make this a modular chassis. Cloud management requires a supported software release, onboarding mode, and licensing.

24 multigigabit copper ports support 100M/1G/2.5G/5G/10G. 560W PoE budget with one default PWR-C1-1100WAC-P PSU. Cisco UPOE is up to 60W per port, not 90W UPOE+. C9300-NM-8X uplinks are optional. Cloud management depends on software, onboarding mode, and licensing.

MS130-24P has 1G SFP uplinks, not 10G SFP+. The -24X model is a different mixed-speed SKU. Dashboard virtual stacking is configuration grouping, not a physical stack. Requires a Meraki management license.

740W published PoE/PoE+ budget for the -48FP SKU. Four 1/10G SFP+ uplinks and two dedicated stack ports; stacking bandwidth is 80 Gbps. Requires a Meraki management license. Check current lifecycle and software support before procurement.

JL725A is the 24G Class 4 PoE, 4SFP+, 370W fixed-power SKU. VSF supports up to eight members and consumes uplink ports. Aruba Central cloud management requires the appropriate subscription. OEM document delivery can vary by region.

JL663A is the 48-port non-PoE model, with four SFP56 uplinks. The M denotes modular power and fans, not a modular line-card chassis. PSU selection is separate. VSF uses uplink ports; supported optics, speeds, and features depend on software. Aruba Central requires licensing.

740W PoE with one 920W AC PSU; up to 1440W with two. The four 10/25G SFP28 ports default to Virtual Chassis and can instead be Ethernet uplinks; do not count them simultaneously for both roles. Mist Wired Assurance requires an appropriate subscription.

48 SFP25 access ports and eight QSFP100 ports. This is a data-center leaf switch, not a copper PoE access switch. MLAG provides multi-chassis link aggregation, not a single-control-plane stack. Port speeds and breakout modes depend on transceivers and EOS support.
